title: Winners have brutal drawdowns

body: Fifteen winners reached trailing P/E ≥70 at the end of their up-move: Bajaj Finance 121 (2021), Astral 118, Pidilite 93, Deepak 93, Dixon 197, Tata Elxsi 103, KPIT 86, Trent 232, Cochin 95, Kaynes 203, CDSL 76, Symphony 84, Page 81, La Opala 70, Alkyl 76. Price change from that peak to 19 Nov 2026: Symphony −74%, KPIT −72%, Tata Elxsi −64%, Alkyl −64%, Kaynes −62%, Cochin −60%, Astral −48%, La Opala −48%, Deepak −46%, Page −42%, Trent −41%, Dixon −29%, CDSL −27%, Pidilite +28%, Bajaj Finance +39%. Median −48%; 13 of 15 negative. The two positive cases still underperformed their own EPS growth, which was 2x and 4.8x. Winners that peaked at 40–60x (Eicher 51, Balkrishna 49, HAL 49, Mazagon 52, Polycab 59, Garware 42, Avanti 45, Caplin 69) did better, with a median of about −25% and several recovering to new highs. The trigger was almost always P/E ≥70 combined with decelerating EPS (Page FY23, Astral FY22–26, Elxsi FY26, Trent LFL, Alkyl spreads, KPIT Europe). Rule for memory: P/E ≥70 alone is not a sell signal (Trent 2020 at 155 worked because EPS was depressed), but P/E ≥70 with the first quarter of EPS deceleration has a poor base rate. Trim rather than hope.
title: After a run ends at P/E ≥70: 13 of 15 Indian winners are lower 2–5 years later (median −48%)

body: This extends insight:us-insider-buying-evidence (Lakonishok-Lee 2001; Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski 2012). Jeng, Metrick and Zeckhauser, 'Estimating the Returns to Insider Trading: A Performance-Evaluation Perspective' (Review of Economics and Statistics 85(2), 2003; ~570 citations), US 1975-1996: a value-weighted portfolio that holds the stocks insiders buy for six months earns abnormal returns of about 6% a year. About a quarter of that accrues in the first five days and about half in the first month after the trade. The portfolio of insider SALES earns no significant abnormal return. Seyhun (1986, 1998) earlier found that top executives' and large trades are more informative than small trades by peripheral insiders. Replicated: yes, across US data (and the UK, Germany and other markets); the purchase/sale asymmetry is robust, since insiders sell for liquidity and diversification but buy for one reason. India: rigorous academic evidence on SEBI PIT (Reg 7) disclosures is thin and we found no high-citation study, so treat the transfer as a hypothesis. Indian promoter buying differs from US insider buying: promoters may creep up via SAST to consolidate control, buy before a delisting or open offer, or support a pledged stock's price. Use for us: weight open-market promoter or KMP purchases that are large relative to holdings, made by several insiders, not ESOP or inter-se transfers, and not linked to pledge top-ups; then check the after-trade holding in the NSE PIT feed. Build our own dataset and measure 6- and 12-month excess returns before treating it as an edge.
title: Insider trading returns, extended: Jeng-Metrick-Zeckhauser (2003) ~6%/yr on purchases, sales ~0; what transfers to India
